# 1 Overview

## 1.1 Objectives

The location choices of businesses play a pivotal role in shaping urban development, influencing economic growth, job creation, and the provision of resources and services. Strategic siting not only creates competitive advantages and supports efficient supply chains, but also contributes to a city’s identity through specialized districts and accessible infrastructure.

Studying the spatio-temporal patterns of new businesses is therefore essential, as it highlights how economic activity and urban forms evolve over time. Such analysis enables urban planners to anticipate growth, identify clusters and trends, improve resource allocation, and design more sustainable and livable cities.

In this exercise, the focus is on new business entities established in Singapore during the first six months of 2025. The objectives are:

• To analyze the “where” and “when” of new business establishments, uncovering spatial clusters, temporal trends, and development hotspots.

• To explore complex interaction patterns beyond simple density measures, such as the clustering of related firms, path-dependency of business locations, and structural changes in commercial areas.
